title: Never pass AI classmates off as peers
statement: Don't present AI classmates as real peers, since learners got better at unmasking them through social and contextual inconsistency rather than language.
detail: Notes on AI classmates cite the one study measuring this directly for school-age students in a live multi-agent setting: detection accuracy improved with repeated exposure, and learners moved from analysing language patterns early to shared social and contextual signals later (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/idea-02-ai-classmates-multi-agent-debate.md`, lines 119-123). The notes recommend designing for social and contextual consistency across repeated sessions, giving each voice a stable memory of earlier sessions (line 141). The project's synthesis adds that AI classmates should take the questioning half of productive talk and not be marketed as real peers, since visual style alone won't stop the fake read (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/IDEA-SYNTHESIS.md`, line 19).
against: The evidence is one field study, with middle-school students rather than Grade 9 (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/idea-02-ai-classmates-multi-agent-debate.md`, lines 119-123). That study used text and game interaction, not synchronised voice and image (lines 152-153).

evidence.quote: detection accuracy improved with repeated exposure, and the strategy shifted from analyzing language patterns early to using shared social/contextual signals later
Use AI classmates for the **questioning** half of productive talk; don't market them as real peers.
Children get better at unmasking AI classmates over sessions, from **social and contextual inconsistency** rather than language (2026 DoppelBot study).
give each expert a stable memory of prior sessions, since that is specifically what let students unmask AI agents with exposure.

citations.ref: Schumacher et al. 2026, Detecting AI Impostors (DoppelBot)
